stage: Textured working-port motion study with readable forward-and-away ship departures
review_method: Full-resolution 1920x1080 final scene frames at output indices 0,48,95 inspected.
Both encoded movies played at normal speed in the Codex in-app browser through a temporary loopback-only server; video-frame callbacks and browser playback quality recorded.
Browser screenshots sampled actual playback and completed playback. This is not a frame-by-frame perceptual inspection of all encoded frames.
findings: Hound and Venture travel bow-first screen-right and recede while the port passes aft; the end views clearly reduce their apparent size.

Venture moves 197 pixels right and shrinks to 76 percent width; Hound moves 166 pixels right and shrinks to 69 percent, with fixed source orientation and conservative clearance through all 96 sampled times.
The paved perimeter meets adjoining terrain without the former detached bright strip in reviewed frames; geometry and negative-control evidence are separate.
Near buildings, tanks, roads and three road vehicles provide distinct parallax depths; vehicle visibility is at least one readable throughout, at least two in85of96 samples.
Architecture finish is limited to fully covered near-object faces; whole-face material fallback avoids projected cabin fragments or an internal projection-edge seam.
rejected_studies: Grounded v1/v2 cards passed midpoint foot-anchor arithmetic but failed moving-camera visual contact. They are not accepted ground-contact technique.
Architecture projection onto clipped or rear faces produced cabin-frame contamination and ship ghosts; final build limits whole-face coverage and source Y<=650.

The first airborne pass used 50/85 metres of source-X motion while the camera advanced 413 metres. Both vessels moved backward across the window; independent keyframes and engine glow did not establish readable departure.
limits: Fixed-aspect ship imagery is not coherent rotating hull geometry, and does not establish landing or contact mechanics.
Large aprons, native-material building faces and simple distant structures retain a visible model-based study character; finer art direction remains reviewable.
Painted card lighting does not dynamically relight; background geography and vessel dimensions/speeds are authored.
Twelve-second cut contains editorial time gaps and retains the forest shot's warmer/wider cabin treatment; no narration, audio or game playback integration.

The departure paths are shot-authored at about 222/261 m/s; painted fixed aspects approximate 8.0/6.7 degrees of viewpoint change. This does not establish general 3D vessel geometry or canonical flight performance.
